sentences.text: 1) To issue a writ in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugnedorder dated 02.04.2024 (Annexure P-12) passed in OriginalApplication No. 200/00071/2020 by Central AdministrativeTribunal Jabalpur.
2)To Call for the entire material/record pertaining to instant controversy from the office of the respondent no. 2 and 3 for its kind perusal.

3) To issue the writ of mandamus to Direct the respondents to consider the case of the Petitioner and provide the employment under the scheme formulated for employment in lieu of land acquired in pay band -1 Rs.5200- 20200 grade pay Rs.
1800/- asper his eligibility and suitability.
4) This Hon'ble Court be further pleased to pass such other order(s)as it may deem fit under the circumstances under the case.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner's adoptee Mother, Parvati Bai W/o Ram Gopalbs Billore, was the owner of the residential plot land bearing Khasra No. 352/1, area 0.03 acre, 0.014 hectare, situated at village Mehragaon Teh.
Itarsi, Distt. Hoshangabad and was in possession of the same.

The respondents have sent a proposal to the Collector Hoshangabad for acquisition of land of the village Mehragaon for the purpose of laying a new rail line known as Pawarkheda Station to Jujharpur Station new Broad Gauge Rail Line, Itarsi, North South grade separator, under which the whole plot of the petitioner's adoptee Mother Parvati Bai W/o Ram Gopal Billore bearing Khasra no.
352/1 area 0.03 acre 0.014 hectare 1500 sq. feet was also demarcated for acquisition with some other plot holders.

In view of the proposal, the acquisition proceeding was initiated under the provisions of Right to fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act of 2013').

sentences.text:
The Land Acquisition Officer i.e. Sub NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:874 3 WP-14211-2024 Divisional Officer (Revenue), Itarsi, District Hoshangabad published a primary draft notification under Section 11 (1)
of the Act, 2013 on 20.02.2015.
Thereafter, the authorities have passed an award on 11.07.2017 (Annexure P/2).
As per the award the compensation has been paid to the respective land owners.

3. It is submitted that since the land acquisition has been taken place as per the provisions of Act of 2013, therefore, the petitioner is entitled to all the benefits of rehabilitation resettlement as provided under Sections 31 and 38 of the Act, 2013.

It is further submitted that the respondents have formulated a scheme to provide employment to the dependent of the affected family under the acquisition and on 16.05.2019 (Annexure P/3), a notification has been issued for giving employment to the dependents of the affected family of the respective villages under the said project.

As per the said notification, a member of the affected family fulfilling the criteria and standard was invited to submit application attached with the notification by fulfilling the same under the pay band of Rs.5200-20200 grade Pay 1800/-.
It was mentioned that the person should be holder of the land or his/her son, daughter, husband or wife.
There was a rider also that the person has not got any land from the State Government in lieu of the land acquired.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that under the scheme dated 16/05/2019, the petitioner being an adopted son through a registered Adoption Deed dated 09/05/2005 of affected person Parvati Bai, the adoptee mother of the petitioner, has submitted an application for getting employment on 24/07/2019 (Annexure P/4) with certificates of required educational NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:874 4 WP-14211-2024 qualification i.e. 10th, 12th standard and provisional trade certificate with NOC/Consent letters given by the adoptee mother Parvati Bai.
However, the application submitted by the petitioner has been rejected vide order/letter dated 13.09.2020 (Annexure P/11).

5. After rejection of his application, the petitioner filed an original application i.e. O.A. No.
200/0071/2020, before the Central Administrative Tribunal, Jabalpur, seeking direction to the respondents to consider his case for employment in lieu of land acquisition.

The tribunal has dismissed the application of the petitioner vide order dated 02.04.2024 (Annexure P/12) on the ground that for valid adoption, there is a requirement of the actual adoption i.e there should be some overt act which signifies the actual delivery of the child and the applicant was not actually given and taken in adoption dated 09.05.2005.
6.

It is submitted by the learned senior counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner, being an adopted son of the affected landlady, has all the required qualifications for getting employment under the scheme.

The residential plot of the petitioner's adoptive mother was acquired and taken into possession in 2017; therefore, the respondents ought to have followed the provisions of Section 38 of the Act of 2013.
However, the respondents arbitrarily and malafidely rejected the application on 13.9.2019 and denied the benefit of employment.

7 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents has submitted that the application for appointment was moved by the petitioner after the date of withdrawal of the policy; therefore, he is not entitled to claim appointment.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:874 5 WP-14211-2024

Further, as per the High School Certificate examination (10+2) in 2009 petitioner's biological father and mother are Bharat Singh Bhaisare and Smt. Rambai Bhaisare and under section 11(iv) of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 (for brevity 'Act,1956'), the child must be actually given and taken in adoption. Section 11 of the Act, 1956 determines whether valid adoption has been made or not.

However, the petitioner has not demonstrated anywhere as to how the adoption deed is valid and adopted child shall be deemed to be the child of his or her adoptive father or mother for all purposes with effect from the date of adoption and in fact the present petitioner was not actually given or taken in adoption.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for appointment.

It is submitted that the Tribunal after considering all aspects of the matter for valid adoption has reached to the conclusion that physical act of giving and receiving of the child is necessary to the validity of an adoption as it is an absolute condition and mere expression or execution of a deed will not operate as valid adoption.

The Tribunal has rightly dismissed the application of the petitioner on the ground that for valid adoption, there is a requirement of actual adoption, i.e. there should be some overt act which signifies the actual delivery of the child and the applicant was not actually given and taken in adoption dated 9.5.2005.
Thus, no case is made out warranting interference.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. The respondent/Railways, vide notification dated 16.05.2019, has issued a benevolent scheme of providing employment to the families affected by the acquisition for laying rail line of the Railways.

The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:874 6 WP-14211-2024 parameters to consider the applications for employment have been framed whereby the applicant should either be owner or son/daughter/husband/wife whose land or part of the land has been acquired by which the family has been affected with the caveat that such person has not received any land in lieu of such land.
10. From the perusal of the record, it is found that the adoptive parents of the petitioners of both the petitions were holding plot of only 1500 sq.ft.
It is clear from the size of the plot that the petitioners were not cultivating over the said plot or it was the only source of livelihood of the petitioners.
The petitioners have already suitably compensated under the Act, 2013.
The scheme is discretionary in nature to be implemented by considering the parameters and the financial impact of acquisition over the families.
Therefore, the petitioners cannot claim as an absolute right to have employment as per the scheme.

It is also found from the record that the scheme announced by way of notification dated 16.05.2019 has been withdrawn vide Board letter dated 11.11.2019 i.e. within six months of the announcement of the scheme.

The respondent/Railways has filed reply stating therein that due to formulation of such scheme, about 1.64 lakhs land losers have become prospective claimants of the railway job and some data has also been submitted in regard to the vacancy and the total employment generated by the Railways.
Accordingly, pleaded that due to such scheme, jobs cannot be granted to all the land losers.

11. It is also observed by the Tribunal that even after the adoption deed was executed, the names of the biological fathers of the petitioners appeared NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:874 7 WP-14211-2024 in the mark sheet and other relevant records.
Meaning thereby that such adoption has not been implemented in the record after its execution.

Considering these facts, the Tribunal has rejected the Original Application and did not interfere with the order dated 13.09.2019 (Annexure P/11).
12.

This Court, on perusal of the record and the scheme, is of the considered opinion that the scheme has been formulated only for the purpose of giving benefit to those persons, who are affected by the acquisition.

From the bare perusal of the documents of plot of the alleged parents of the petitioners,
it is found that the plot size is only of 1500 sq. ft., which cannot be said to be source of livelihood for the affected family.

In the discretion of the Railways, the applications of the petitioners have been rejected finding that even after execution of the adoption deed the names of biological fathers of the petitioners have continued to be recorded in the record.
This Court does not find any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitions sans merit and are hereby dismissed.
(VIVEK RUSIA)
